description: A broken hash algorithm, judged by what the digest is asked to establish rather than by its name. The algorithm is still read from a literal and an algorithm chosen at runtime is still not guessed at; what decides now is the second line, where the digest is compared against a value the program was given. Two digests are compared and are findings: MD5 verifying downloaded bytes and SHA-1 verifying a claimed signature, both computed a function away from the comparison. Five digests are silent, and each one is a different edge of the same judgement: SHA-256 compared the same way (not broken), HMAC-SHA1 compared the same way (its soundness is the key and the construction, not collision resistance), an algorithm that is a parameter (not knowable), and MD5 with no comparison at all (a cache key is a name for a slot, and a collision there costs a miss). The finding lands at the comparison because that is where the program decides something -- the constructor is where it would be fixed, and the evidence names both.

expected.note: the digest stands in for the bytes it was computed from, and a second input that hashes the same passes this check
a bare SHA-1 digest verified against a claimed one, unlike the HMAC-SHA1 below which is silent
